text:
Priya (product-security): ok team — planning Q4 work for keystore/KMS + retention. need to pick priorities that let us close the SOC2 gap and give customers predictable options. thoughts?

Mike (eng-platform): +1. are we prioritizing HSM integration or flexible retention policy first? both are fairly big.

Anna (secops): SOC2 auditors flagged both: key custody controls (KMS/HSM) and inconsistent audit log retention. auditors want tamper-evident logs + retention policy aligned to customer SLA tiers.

Chris (infra): HSM integration has infra lead time (procurement / modules) but we can ship a soft HSM abstraction that supports external KMS for private deployments sooner.

Priya (product-security): proposal: split into two tracks — short (Q4 sprint 1): audit-log retention policy + configurable retention UI + enforcement hooks; medium (Q4 sprint 2): KMS abstraction + pluggable HSM adapter; long: on-prem HSM appliance onboarding. ok?

Mike (eng-platform): that sounds reasonable. for sprint 1 we need clear launch criteria. suggested: (1) retention config per org, (2) server-side enforcement, (3) migration job for existing logs, (4) docs + opt-in telemetry.

Anna (secops): add: retention verification tests and a rolling audit to prove data is purged when TTL expires. also retention != deletion for backups — need retention tags applied to backups and snapshots.

Chris (infra): technical tradeoff: immediate deletion of logs has replication concerns. better to mark as expired and schedule deletion job with idempotency. sample cron: ```bash
# purge expired logs
redis-cli ZRANGEBYSCORE audit_logs -inf $(date +%s) | xargs -n1000 rm -f || true
```
Not final, but shows approach.

Priya (product-security): good — include backup/snapshot tagging in the spec. also need to define customer-facing SLA matrix: 30d/90d/365d options and enterprise custom retention. link to mock UI: /console/settings/security/retention (design PR coming).

Mike (eng-platform): owners? Anna + Chris for infra enforcement, Mike to own API/config, Priya to own product acceptance and SOC2 checklist items. Can we get a rough ETA?

Anna (secops): ETA sprint 1 (4 weeks) for retention policy + verification harness if we staff 2 engineers. I'm going to draft acceptance tests for SOC2 appendix: evidence artifacts, retention test plan, and a runbook.

Chris (infra): ETA sprint 2 (6 weeks) for KMS adapter prototype that supports AWS KMS + Vault + mock-HSM. full HSM integration depends on procurement, vendor tests.

Priya (product-security): launch criteria checklist (WIP):
- retention config in console (yes/no)
- server-side enforcement active in prod (smoke pass)
- automated retention verification job + recorded run (evidence)
- docs + customer migration notes
- SOC2 evidence folder populated for auditor review
- API docs for KMS adapter (alpha)

Jira Bot: Created ticket SEC-612: "Retention policy enforcement + verification" assigned to Anna; link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-612

Mike (eng-platform): blockers: db migration for retention index, migration window needs low-latency strategy. can we use background migrator with throttling?

Anna (secops): we'll flag migration as a canary rollout. acceptance gated by retention verification results for the canary org. if fail, rollback and revert retention enforcement.

Priya (product-security): decision: move forward with sprint 1 retention deliverable as highest priority for SOC2 readiness. sprint 2 will start KMS adapter design in parallel but limited engineer allocation. I'll update OKR mapping: this maps to Security OKR Q4.r1 and Platform reliability objective.

Chris (infra): noted. I'll add a risk row for snapshot retention mismatch and mitigation (snapshot tags + periodic verification).

Mike (eng-platform): sounds good. I'll spin up the RFC doc and add rough WBS. PRD owners — Priya for product, Anna for security, Chris for infra, Mike for platform.

Priya (product-security): thanks — can everyone add time estimates to SEC-612/SEC-613 by EOD tomorrow? I'll synthesize into roadmap and present at leadership sync Friday. :thumbsup:
